mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in the majority of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals an overheating labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signal an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in the majority of periods when RSAFS growth is positive, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,100,000 units signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 1100.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Federal Funds Rate above 0.5% signals a shift to tighter monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.0%), a decline in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in high-unemployment periods when PAYEMS growth rate < -0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
